Hi Mike, 


I am having some trouble with the mcera5 function. I’m trying to run the following: 

 

  file_path <-path.expand('~ /era5')

  dfinish <-"12/05/2020"

  dstart <-"12/01/2020"

  x <- -81.59591

  y <- 36.62719

 

  loc <- c(x, y) 

 

  str(list(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, 

           dem.res = 100,

           Usrhyt = 0.03,

           spatial = file_path))

  

 

  micro<-micro_era5(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish, 

                    dem.res = 100,

                    Usrhyt = 0.03,

                    spatial = file_path)

ℹ In argument: `lsm = dplyr::case_when(lsm < 0 ~ 0, lsm >= 0 ~ lsm)`.

Caused by error in `dplyr::case_when()`:

! Failed to evaluate the left-hand side of formula 1.

Caused by error:

! object 'lsm' not found

Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.

> rlang::last_trace()

Caused by error:

! object 'lsm' not found

     ▆

 14. │     └─mask$eval_all_mutate(quo)

 15. │       └─dplyr (local) eval()

 16. └─dplyr::case_when(lsm < 0 ~ 0, lsm >= 0 ~ lsm)

 17.   └─dplyr:::case_formula_evaluate(...)

 18.     ├─base::withCallingHandlers(...)

 19.     └─rlang::eval_tidy(pair$lhs, env = default_env)

 

 

Running rlang::last_trace() reveals that the error occurs in the nc_to_df subfunction. I have attempted to dig into this further but am unsure where the ‘lsm’ variable is supposed to come from. Is it suppose to be part of the NetCDF file? 

 

The NetCDF file was downloaded using the build_era5_request function (see attached). I’ve updated/unistalled-and-reinstalled all necessary packages.

 

R version 4.4.1 (2024-06-14)

Running under: macOS Sonoma 14.5

NicheMapR_3.3.2

mcera5_0.4.0

 

Could you please help me understand where ‘lsm’ is defined or why this error might be occurring?

 

Thank you!

messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: Re: Trouble with nc_to_df subfunction in mcera5 in NicheMapR
parts:
Hi Morgan,

Yep, mcera5 is my jurisdiction. `lsm` is the land-sea mask, which is used to identify land vs sea pixels; this is then used to perform a correction to capture coastal effects, which ERA5 doesn't handle that well out of the box.

Inspecting your netCDF (era5_2020.nc), indeed the lsm variable is missing – if you queried via mcera5 then I'm not sure how this ended up missing, but perhaps your query was during the flurry of ERA5 moving from ECMWF's old Climate Data Store to the new Climate Data Store, during which some variable names changed, etc.

The best solution is to re-query your ERA5 data now that you have the most updated version of mcera5. You can also download just `lsm` by going to this page, checking "land-sea mask" under the "Other" section, checking "netCDF4" under "Data Format", and matching the spatial and temporal extent of your existing netCDF. You could then combine the two netCDFs via NCO, ncdf4, or terra functions.

If it's a pain to re-query your ERA5 data, or you don't care about the coastal correction, here's a quick fix to work with your netCDF as-is without lsm: fork the GitHub repository dklinges9/mcera5, and in internal.R delete the comma at the end of line 181, and delete lines 182 - 184 and lines 186 - 189. Then install your forked version of the package. This removes the dependency on lsm and micro_era5 should work with your data.

Note that because the new Climate Data Store has a lower API limit than previously, build_request_era5() by default queries ERA5 data by monthly chunks, and then request_era5() by default combines these monthly chunks into an annual file (which is more convenient for eg NicheMapR::micro_era5). This keeps far more ERA5 queries below their API limit (depending on your spatial extent). This lower API limit is a bit of a pain for us, but I'm hoping it's just temporary as ECMWF wraps up their move to the new Climate Data Store.

Feel free to reach out if you have other issues. A lot of mcera5 users reach out directly to me but for cases like this I think it makes sense to parasitize the NicheMapR Google Group given micro_era5()'s reliance on mcera5.

Cheers,
Dave
